reviewer: adversarial finder (score not authoritative; see PROMPT-STANDARD "How to review a prompt")

gaps.property: Property 3 (numeric) / module-spec rule 2 (world data and derivations) — self-contradictory: acceptance criteria 2 and 12 are arithmetically unsatisfiable for 4 of the 12 views
gaps.problem: §2.1 rows 5-8 source education, health, fire and crime straight from the building record, but `services` is a stub, so simulation/economy.js:424 sets r.education = 0 and r.health = 0 for EVERY building whenever servicesActive() is false (simulation/index.js:119 requires world.services.items.size > 0, and the stub's place() returns null). The education and health grids are therefore constant 0: criterion 2's `p95 - p5 >= 0.25` is impossible and criterion 12's coveredFraction is 0, below the [0.25, 0.80] band. In the same branch r.crime is one city-wide number for every building and r.fireRisk is 0.1/0.3 by type, so their service term (1 - value) is >= 0.5 almost everywhere and coveredFraction lands near 1.0, above the band. §2.1's S(kind) fallback is wired only into rows 9-11, and criterion 2 says flatly that 'no data was available' is never an accepted answer. The builder must invent a fallback the spec claims to have removed, and the critic will fail four views the builder believes it built to spec — one full round.
gaps.fix: Extend the S(kind) fallback into rows 5-8 with fixed expressions, e.g. education = clamp01(max(r.education, S('school')*0.5 + S('high_school')*0.3 + S('university')*0.2)), health likewise from clinic/hospital, crime = clamp01(0.55 - 0.5*S('police') + 0.15*(density==='high')), fire = clamp01(0.45 + 0.25*(type==='industrial') - 0.5*S('fire')); add school, clinic, police and fire to the 8 fallback sources in §8 item 4 and criterion 12, and state the source-kind -> view mapping per row so the coveredFraction band is reachable by construction.

gaps.property: Module-spec rule 7 (dependencies and their REAL APIs) — a named API's signature is wrong and its module is misdescribed
gaps.problem: §7 and §6 both say `traffic` is a stub and that 'there is no flowGrid()'. traffic is implemented (244 lines) and src/modules/traffic/index.js:133 defines flowGrid() returning an OBJECT — {size:256, cellSize, data:Float32Array, sample(x,z)} — not a grid array. §2.1 row 1 says 'if present (copy, it is already 256²)', so a builder who follows the spec literally copies an object where a Float32Array is expected and silently ships a zero/NaN traffic grid that fails criterion 2, or writes a fallback path they were told is the only path. The spec also does not note that traffic is absent from `dependencies`, so the real grid appears only under --showcase all and never in the graded showcase shots.
gaps.fix: Replace the traffic entry with the real signature: `flowGrid() -> {size:256, cellSize:8, data:Float32Array(65536), sample(x,z)}` (traffic/index.js:133), say to copy `.data` and clamp01 it, and add one line that traffic is not a declared dependency so the fallback in row 1 is what runs in every infoviews showcase shot; correct the §6 bullet to name only `services` as a stub.

gaps.property: Property 3 (numeric) / Property 4 (anchored) — the derivation table's own promise ('two builders must ship the same heatmap') is broken in row 1
gaps.problem: Row 1's fallback congestion is `clamp01(betweenness(e) / (types[e.type].lanes * 380) * activity(hour))`, but `betweenness(e)` is never defined anywhere in the spec or the codebase — no node set, no path metric (hops vs. edge.length), no weighting, no normalisation. Its magnitude is entirely implementation-dependent, which makes the divisor 380 meaningless and the fixed domain ('0 = free flow, 1 = gridlock') unenforceable. Two competent builders produce visibly different traffic heatmaps, and the critic cannot tell which is correct.
gaps.fix: Define it exactly in row 1, e.g.: 'betweenness(e) = the number of all-pairs shortest paths over world.roads.nodes that traverse e, computed by Dijkstra with cost = edge.length over every ordered node pair, divided by (N-1)(N-2); N = nodes.size'. Then restate the 380 constant as calibrated against that definition, and give the expected p95 for the staged city so the builder can check the scaling.

gaps.property: Property 1 (sequenced) / Property 5 (bounded blast radius) — the declared budget conflicts with core and with ARCHITECTURE
gaps.problem: §5 declares budget.drawCalls = 8. src/core/constants.js:23 sets BUDGET.perModuleDrawCalls.infoviews = 5 and ARCHITECTURE §15 specifies 'one full-screen decal/texture per view, <= 5 draw calls' for the whole module. CRITIC.md's pass condition is 'draw calls within the declared budget' while its calibration step is ARCHITECTURE §9/§12 — so the critic can legitimately fail the module at 8 draws while criterion 17 passes it. The spec attributes '(ARCHITECTURE §15)' to 'ground <= 5', which silently reinterprets §15's module-wide ceiling as a ground-layer ceiling. The builder cannot fix this: constants.js is core.
gaps.fix: Say so explicitly in §5: '§15's 5 covers the ground decal only; tint (1) + network (2) need perModuleDrawCalls.infoviews raised to 8 — file that exact change in docs/core-requests/infoviews.md in round 1', and make filing it an acceptance item so the critic grades the reconciliation rather than the conflict.

gaps.property: Rules for role prompts (invariants live in the role file) — duplicated critic content that has already drifted
gaps.problem: §8 states 'Critics shoot aerial, street, skyline, closeup x 06.5, 12, 17.5, 22, plus the six presets at 12 and 22' and criterion 23 requires 'zero console errors in all 16 gauntlet shots'. CRITIC.md's actual command is `gauntlet.mjs --times 12,22` (8 shots) plus two single golden-hour shots, and docs/STATUS.json's core note records that the matrix was deliberately reduced to '8 shots + 2 golden-hour + presets' for throughput on this 4-CPU SwiftShader box. PROMPT-STANDARD rule 8 itself says '12 and 22 plus golden hour'. So the spec demands evidence the critic will not produce, and it duplicates role-file content that has already drifted once.
gaps.fix: Delete the matrix from §8 and rewrite criterion 23 as 'zero console errors and modules.infoviews.status === ready in every shot the critic takes per CRITIC.md, plus the six declared presets at 12 and 22, the 1280x720 shot and the --showcase all shot'. Keep §8's per-camera 'how it must read' prose, which is the part that belongs in a module spec.

gaps.property: Property 4 (anchored) — the visual target and the graded number describe two different looks
gaps.problem: §3 describes cs2_7 correctly as 'the data is opaque, flat and saturated', 'a single pure yellow', 'There is no pastel wash' — and I confirmed the reference's factories are fully painted. It then imports cs2_1's translucent road-preview film and criterion 7 grades building tint at `a` in [0.55, 0.75]. A 0.55 film over a grey facade is much closer to the pastel wash §3 bans than to the reference it points at, and it works against criterion 5 (top-decile overlay saturation >= 0.45 and >= 2.0x the world) and criterion 7's own >= 25/255 roof-vs-wall step, since the fixed top-light term only supplies a 0.28 multiplicative difference on the tint's contribution. A builder can satisfy criterion 7 and still be told the frame does not look like cs2_7.
gaps.fix: Give one alpha per layer and reconcile the references in one sentence: ground overlay opaque over land (a >= 0.85, water clause unchanged), building tint a in [0.55, 0.75] because facade legibility (cs2_1) is deliberately preferred over the reference's opaque paint. Then state the ramp's minimum luminance so the 25/255 roof/wall step is reachable at the dark end of every one of the 12 ramps.

gaps.property: Property 2 (falsifiable) — the module's central visual premise is outside its blast radius with no scoring rule
gaps.problem: cs2_7's look depends on the rest of the world being desaturated. §6 forbids faking it (no grey quad, no dome, no fog bump), the module may not edit effects/ or buildings/, and it only publishes world.infoview.desaturation plus a core request. Yet criterion 5 requires overlay saturation >= 2.0x the non-overlay pixels in a fully saturated frame, and CRITIC.md scores 0-10 against CS2 where the world is grey. Criterion 3 has exactly the right device for this (record the night-luminance drop as a diagnostic owned by environment/effects, not an infoviews fail) but it is not applied to desaturation.
gaps.fix: Add the same clause to §4: 'the grey world is owned by effects and buildings; with desaturation unhonoured the reference cannot be matched — record the measured saturation ratio and log the unhonoured uniform in docs/core-requests/infoviews.md; it is not an infoviews fail', and state the ceiling score that is reachable without it so the critic and builder do not argue about the gap.

gaps.property: Module-spec rule 2 (copy the signatures, do not paraphrase) — a citation that does not match the cited lines
gaps.problem: §2.1 row 4 says the happiness derivation uses 'the terms economy.js:318-321 uses globally' and then gives 0.14*education + 0.12*health + 0.10*parks - 0.16*crime + 0.10*landValue - 0.22*pollution - 0.10*noise. Lines 318-321 actually read civic = 0.10*education + 0.08*health + 0.06*parks + 0.06*police + 0.04*fire - 0.14*(1-power) - 0.14*(1-water) - 0.05*(1-garbage) - 0.02, folded into hTarget. None of the spec's coefficients appear there. The formula is complete enough to build from, but a builder who does what BUILDER.md tells them (read the dependency's code) will find the citation false and be tempted to 'correct' the numbers, and two builders will then disagree.
gaps.fix: Drop the citation and say what it is: 'a per-building analogue of the city-wide happiness term, coefficients fixed here and deliberately not identical to economy.js's civic expression — do not re-derive them from the code.'

gaps.property: Property 3 (numeric) — a graded threshold the builder cannot control
gaps.problem: Criterion 6 requires >= 5 of 8 equal-width L* buckets each holding >= 2% of overlay pixels in iv_landvalue_12.png. §2.1 forbids renormalising (fixed domain per view) and the ramp is hud.js's three-stop landvalue gradient, so the L* histogram is a function of simulation's landValue distribution — a dependency the builder does not own and which criterion 2 constrains only to p95 - p5 >= 0.25. A perfectly built ramp over a grid concentrated in 0.3-0.6 occupies about 3 buckets and fails a criterion that exists to grade the ramp.
gaps.fix: Split it: keep the 5-sample adjacent-colour test (>= 40/255) as the ramp check, and grade band legibility on the ramp LUT plus a data-side requirement the builder can meet — e.g. 'choose ramp stops so that the 5th-95th percentile of the view's fixed domain spans >= 45 L*', with the bucket test applied to the LUT sampled at the grid's percentile distribution rather than to raw pixel counts.

gaps.property: Property 2 (falsifiable) — the four remaining items a critic cannot mechanically check
gaps.problem: (a) Criterion 21 probes 'material.uniforms.uMix (or equivalent)' — 'or equivalent' means the critic has to reverse-engineer the builder's uniform naming to grade the transition. (b) Criterion 20 requires recompute 'at most once per game hour ... coalesced by >= 0.1 s, never per frame' with no clock domain (wall-clock would collide with BUILDER.md's Date.now ban and with criterion 19's determinism) and no counter to observe it — api.recompute() returns ms, not a count. (c) Criterion 4 says 'probe 2000 points on the ground overlay's surface' without naming the method (raycast the mesh? read the vertex buffer? call an api?). (d) Criterion 12's '12-25 m soft edge' and criterion 9's 'follows every curve / no un-ribboned wedge' are the eye-graded remnants sitting next to probes that already cover the substance.
gaps.fix: Add `api.transition() -> 0..1` and `api.recomputeCount() -> int` to §2's api list and grade those; state the coalescing window in game-seconds; name criterion 4's method ('raycast ctx.group's ground mesh at 2000 seeded (x,z) and compare hit.y to world.terrain.getHeight'); and mark 12(d) and 9's image clauses explicitly as confirming evidence, not pass conditions, the way criterion 10 already does for its PNG.

strengths: The §4 preamble's A/B overlay-pixel mask is the strongest falsifiability device in this repo's specs: shoot with the view on, call api.setView(null), shoot again, pixel is overlay iff max channel delta > 6/255, plus a 64x36 screenToGround distance JSON and a shipped shots/infoviews/rN/mask.mjs. It converts criteria 3, 5, 6, 10 and 11 from art arguments into a re-runnable segmentation, and it names the consequence of not shipping the mask (graded as failed, not argued).

§3 is faithful to the actual reference. I opened cs2_7.jpg: opaque flat yellow buildings and green network over a grey-white desaturated world, a top-left MAP LEGEND with colour swatch + label + right-aligned 'Building color'/'Network color'/'Terrain color' classifiers and Bad/Good, Low/High gradient bars, and a left-edge icon-tile picker. Every clause in §3 is checkable in a screenshot, and views[].kind:'terrain'|'network'|'building' mirrors the reference's classifier column.

The §2 synchrony contract is derived from real code, not asserted: hud.action() emits {action,args} at hud.js:382, setInfoview calls this.action('infoview',v) at hud.js:954 and this._renderLegend() at hud.js:957, which reads ctx.world.infoview?.legend at hud.js:963 on the same synchronous stack. The spec pre-empts the exact one-frame-late failure it names in §6 and grades it in criterion 15.

Numbers are internally consistent where checked: 256x256 cells x 2 = 131 072 ground triangles; 12 data + 12 LUT + 1 noise = 25 textures under the 26 ceiling; 12 x 256² R32F = 3 MB; RENDER_ORDER.MARKINGS 21 / TRANSPARENT 100 / LAYERS.NO_SHADOW 9 match src/core/constants.js exactly; zoning's real lifts (overlay.js:8-9 LIFT_CELL 0.16, LIFT_LOT 0.26) and polygonOffsetFactor -4/-6 (overlay.js:160,206) are quoted correctly.

Most dependency citations are real and precise: intersections() with arms {edgeId,dir,trim,width,...} at roads/build.js:1231; grids()/building()/services()/activity()/pollutionAt at simulation/index.js:179-216; SERVICE_KEYS at economy.js:69; virtual-building NaN x/z at economy.js:170/178; the splat kernel A*(1-d2)² accumulated at grids.js:38 (matches _splat exactly); world.services.kinds' 17 entries; and the load-bearing claim that core applies ?camera= after showcase.setup (main.js registers presets at :98, applies the preset at :105).

Known failure modes are this project's, not generic: effects_r1 issues 1-2 (washed-out golden hour, milky blue dusk), environment_r2 issues 1/2/4 (milky 17:30, per-pixel static from a hashed varying, grey night), ui_r1 issue 2 and simulation_r1 issue 4 (both lost a round to 720p clipping), roads_r1 issue 1 (protrusion). All verified in docs/critic/.

Blast radius, event contract and role-file hygiene are handled well: writable folder named, ui/buildings/core explicitly off-limits with docs/core-requests/infoviews.md as the route, and criterion 19 deliberately refuses to restate BUILDER.md's Math.random ban and CRITIC.md's grep. Criterion 4's split conformance band is written so §6's ridge-crest fix cannot fail the check it exists to satisfy.
19 of 23 acceptance items are mechanically checkable by probe or by a defined pixel measurement.
verdict: 8.0 — fails at 8.5. This is the most rigorous module spec in the repo and it is close: all ten properties are present, 19 of 23 acceptance items are mechanically checkable, the A/B overlay-pixel mask is a genuinely new falsifiability device, §3 is faithful to the real cs2_7 image, and almost every dependency citation I spot-checked (roads/build.js:1231, simulation/index.js:179-216, economy.js:69/170/178, grids.js:38, hud.js:382/954/957/963, main.js:98 vs 105, constants.js render orders, zoning overlay.js lifts) is exactly right. It fails on Lens 1 and Lens 2 for concrete, cheap-to-fix reasons, not on tone. Lens 1: a builder must guess `betweenness(e)` (undefined), will mis-copy `flowGrid()` (the spec says traffic is a stub with no flowGrid; traffic is real and returns an object, not an array), and must invent the education/health/crime/fire fallback the spec claims to have supplied. Lens 2: criteria 2 and 12 are arithmetically unsatisfiable for four of the twelve views with `services` stubbed — economy.js:424 zeroes education and health for every building and makes crime uniform, so coveredFraction is 0 for two views and ~1.0 for two others against a [0.25, 0.80] band. That single defect is a guaranteed round of builder-versus-critic argument, which is exactly what this standard exists to prevent. Add a budget that contradicts core constants (8 vs BUDGET.perModuleDrawCalls.infoviews = 5), a duplicated critic shot matrix that has already drifted (16 shots vs CRITIC.md's 8+2), and a visual target (opaque data over a desaturated world) that the module is forbidden to achieve with no scoring rule for its absence. Fix gaps 1-5 and this is a 9; gaps 6-10 take it to 9.5.
